risks: carry_forward() checks a node's own subject fingerprint as well as its dependencies. This is stricter than the literal S00 wording ('dependency fingerprints') and is deliberate: promoting a node whose own subject changed would emit a proof claim for changed content, contradicting the canonical invariant that unchanged proofs carry forward by fingerprint.
The legacy bridge is duck-typed so the kernel does not import product modules; a change to the legacy attribute shape would only surface in the A2 suite.
Duplicate ProofState definitions remain in three modules until their own shards migrate them.
